C0.quote: take an approval profile as input and decide on an axis
C0.note: Borderline: axis rules aggregate voters' approval ballots into a collective output (an axis), studied axiomatically with social choice methods; the output is an ordering summarising the data rather than a winner, and the paper notes the data may be any binary evaluation data. Coded ELIG because the rule aggregates several voters' ballots and the paper frames it in voting terms (political elections, Supreme Court votes).

C1.loc: Abstract, p. 2757; Sec. 4 Theorem 1, p. 2760; Sec. 5, pp. 2760-2761; Sec. 6, pp. 2761-2763
C1.quote: compare 5 different axis selection rules axiomatically
C1.note: AX: Propositions 2-8, Theorems 2-3. AL: Theorem 1 (NP-completeness). SI: Sec. 6.1 synthetic noise models. EM: Sec. 6.2 Voter Autrement data and Sec. 6.3 Supreme Court data.

C2.1.quote: An approval profile P is a collection of n approval ballots

C2.2.quote: An approval ballot is a non-empty subset of candidates
C2.2.note: Ranking-based comparison rules (VD-rank, FT-rank) from prior work are used only as benchmarks in Sec. 6; the paper's own rules take approval ballots.

C2.3.quote: Each voter v estimates the position of each candidate
C2.3.note: In the noisy observation model voters have positions p(v) and noisy estimates of candidate positions, from which approval sets are derived. Sec. 4 (p. 2759) also refers to a voter not approving a candidate they do not know as an error.

C2.4.quote: Voters approve (resp. rank) candidates based on their estimations.
C2.4.note: Positions p(v) and estimates p_v(c) have separate notation from the approval set; Sec. 4 p. 2759 also says a missing approval may be an error ('a voter i might not approve a candidate c because i does not know who c is'). In the axiomatic part, ballots are taken as given.

C3.1.quote: Voters approve (resp. rank) candidates based on their estimations.
C3.1.note: No analysis considers strategic misreporting; voter behaviour is only modelled as a fixed noisy generative process in Sec. 6.1.

C3.2.loc: Checked: Abstract; Sec. 1 Introduction; Sec. 3 Preliminaries; Sec. 4 Axis Rules; Sec. 5; Sec. 6 Experiments; Sec. 7 Future Work
C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitudes (sincerely/truthfully); the synthetic model generates approvals from noisy estimates of positions, which is a generative model rather than a sincerity statement.

C4.1.note: The only utility-type term is 'cost', used for the cost a ballot incurs under an axis, a goodness-of-fit measure of the axis rather than a voter's utility, welfare or disutility; no utility, welfare, satisfaction or distortion of voters is used. Applicability condition judged not met.

C4.2.note: 'Dichotomous preferences' appears only in titles of cited works in the reference list, not in the paper's own text.

C5.1.quote: measured the distance of a rule’s output to the ground truth
C5.1.note: Rules are evaluated by Kendall-tau distance to ground-truth or reference axes and by fraction of voters whose ballots are intervals, not by welfare, efficiency, satisfaction, representation, proportionality or distortion.

VOT.quote_behav: Voters approve (resp. rank) candidates based on their estimations.
VOT.note: Voters act only by submitting approval ballots, given exogenously in the axiomatic part and generated by a fixed noisy rule in the synthetic model.

CAN.note: Candidates are only alternatives placed on the axis.

ORG.note: No organiser acts in the model.

DES.note: Rule choice is discussed via axioms, but no designer's choice or objective is modelled.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: Our rules will find an axis in a principled way.
We do not identify any positive features of Minimum Flips.
Voter Deletion and Ballot Completion satisfy a desirable monotonicity property

C9.1.note: Claim 1 concerns real practice (pollsters' ad hoc axes in French election polls); claims 2-3 bear on which axis rule should be used.

C9.2.loc: Abstract, p. 2757; Sec. 6.1 Synthetic Data, p. 2762
C9.2.quote: each voter approves adjacent candidates, an analogue of singlepeakedness
C9.2.note: Claims 2-3 are evaluative readings of axiomatic results and need no further modelling assumption. Claim 1 (that the rules recover an ideological axis for polls) needs that approval ballots reflect proximity on an ideological axis; this is stated in the abstract and formalised in the noisy observation model of Sec. 6.1. No assumption about strategic behaviour, information or utilities is needed.

C10.1.loc: Checked: Abstract; Sec. 1 Introduction; Sec. 3 Preliminaries; Sec. 4; Sec. 7 Future Work
C10.1.note: The paper defines rules as functions of approval profiles but does not state that it studies them only as functions of submitted inputs or takes no position on how inputs relate to held attitudes.
